correctness.rationale: If an ideal has coordinate support J, multiplying its vectors by individual natural-basis vectors shows it contains e_i² for each i in J. These squares are independent by invertibility; dimension comparison forces the ideal to be the coordinate span of J. Thus nonsimplicity is an outgoing zero cut and decomposability is a two-way zero cut. The unique partition into weak components gives the component-of-label-1 recurrence and formal exponential formula. For a fixed size-k cut, block-triangular/block-diagonal enumeration gives g_k g_(n−k) times q^(k(n−k)) or 1, respectively. Intersecting distinct singleton row/column events prescribes at least 2n−3 zeros, and intersecting isolated vertices prescribes 4n−6. Conditioning on invertibility costs at most the inverse of the positive limiting product of (1−q^−j). For larger cuts use k(n−k)−2(n−2)=(k−2)(n−k−2), symmetry, and the geometric bound with ratio n q^(−s(n/2−2)) for s=1 or 2. Together with the exact singleton probabilities and Bonferroni, this yields both errors and the stated conditional ratio. Independent exhaustive prime-field replay reproduced the six recorded cases, including binary n=4 counts 20160, 11658, 19446 (all, simple, indecomposable).
residual_risks: The finite replay checks prime fields only and does not prove any limiting claim. The algebraic proof treats all prime powers with q fixed for the stated asymptotics.
